scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Wotagei originated in the 1970s and 1980s from shin'eitai cheering squads.
The practice of MIX, a patterned call, was established around 1993.
The 2002 song 'Romantic Ukare Mode' became the most associated track with the dance, leading to a viral performance outside the Saitama Super Arena in 2004.
on_screen: Map: Japan · East Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Wotagei is a form of fan support and artistic expression.
It is performed to show dedication to idols, seiyuu (voice actresses), and during anime-related events.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performers, known as uchishi, use glow sticks or penlights to create light trails.
Techniques are divided into chorus-based moves like thundersnake, muramasa, and amaterasu, and non-chorus moves like OAD and PPPH.
Movements involve jumping, clapping, and arm-waving.
Watch for Thundersnake, Romance.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (MuvJR2Pc9Vc)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Requires significant space; often performed at the back of venues.
